---
title: "Signals"
subtitle: "Is any kind of recall more common than its own recent history would predict?"
---

```{r setup}
source(here::here("R", "site_setup.R"))
library(purrr)

# Signal detection uses US CPSC notices only: one regulator, a consistent
# series since 2000, and enough records for a baseline. Canadian counts are
# too small, and start too late, to support it.
us <- recalls |>
  filter(source == "US CPSC", recall_year >= 2000) |>
  mutate(doy = as.integer(format(recall_date, "%j")))

data_to  <- max(recalls$recall_date)
cut_doy  <- as.integer(format(data_to, "%j"))
yrs      <- 2000:this_year
haz_lv   <- c("Fall or crash", "Fire or burn", "Laceration", "Other")
comp_lv  <- us |> count(failed_component, sort = TRUE) |> pull(failed_component)
comp_lv  <- c(setdiff(comp_lv, "Other or unclear"), "Other or unclear")

series_defs <- bind_rows(
  tibble(group = "All", name = "All bicycle recalls"),
  tibble(group = "E-bikes", name = "E-bike related"),
  tibble(group = "Hazard", name = haz_lv),
  tibble(group = "Failed part", name = comp_lv)
)

member <- function(group, name) {
  switch(group,
         "All"         = rep(TRUE, nrow(us)),
         "E-bikes"     = us$is_ebike_related,
         "Hazard"      = us$hazard_group == name,
         "Failed part" = us$failed_component == name)
}

counts <- pmap_dfr(series_defs, function(group, name) {
  m <- member(group, name)
  tibble(group, name, year = yrs,
         full = map_int(yrs, function(y) sum(m & us$recall_year == y)),
         ytd  = map_int(yrs, function(y) sum(m & us$recall_year == y & us$doy <= cut_doy)))
})

# Baseline: the mean of the five previous years. The current, partial year is
# compared year-to-date with the same part of the five previous years.
baseline_years <- 5
min_count      <- 3

assess <- counts |>
  group_by(group, name) |>
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    base_full = map_dbl(year, function(y) mean(full[year >= y - baseline_years & year <= y - 1])),
    base_ytd  = map_dbl(year, function(y) mean(ytd[year >= y - baseline_years & year <= y - 1]))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(year >= 2000 + baseline_years) |>
  mutate(
    is_ytd   = year == this_year,
    observed = if_else(is_ytd, ytd, full),
    expected = if_else(is_ytd, base_ytd, base_full),
    limit95  = qpois(0.95, expected),
    limit99  = qpois(0.99, expected),
    status   = case_when(
      observed >= min_count & observed > limit99 ~ "Signal",
      observed >= min_count & observed > limit95 ~ "Watch",
      TRUE ~ "Expected"
    ),
    label = if_else(is_ytd, paste0(year, " to date"), as.character(year))
  )

recent <- assess |>
  filter(year >= last_full_year, status != "Expected") |>
  arrange(desc(status == "Signal"), group, name)

describe <- function(df) {
  if (nrow(df) == 0) return("no series")
  paste0("**", df$name, "** (", df$status, ": ", df$observed, " against ",
         round(df$expected, 1), " expected, ", df$label, ")", collapse = "; ")
}

n_tests  <- nrow(assess)
n_signal <- sum(assess$status == "Signal")
n_watch  <- sum(assess$status == "Watch")

ojs_define(
  sig = assess |> select(group, name, year, label, observed, expected, limit95, limit99, status, is_ytd),
  smeta = list(series = series_defs$name, groups = series_defs$group,
               dataTo = format(data_to, "%d %B %Y"), thisYear = this_year)
)
```

## How this works

Surveillance systems for infectious disease flag a count when it rises above what the recent past would predict. This page applies the same idea to US bicycle recalls:

- **Baseline.** For each kind of recall and each year, the expected count is the average of the five previous years.
- **Threshold.** A Poisson model gives the range of counts that chance alone would produce around that average. A count above the 95th percentile is marked **Watch**, and a count above the 99th percentile is marked **Signal**. Counts below `r min_count` are never flagged, because one or two recalls are not a pattern.
- **The current year** is incomplete, so it is compared year-to-date: recalls up to `r format(data_to, "%d %B")` this year against the same part of each of the five previous years.

This is the logic of the historical limits method used in routine notifiable disease reporting, adapted to annual counts and small numbers.

## What is flagged now

For `r last_full_year` and `r this_year` to date, the flagged series are: `r describe(recent)`.

Across all `r n_tests` series-year comparisons since 2005, `r n_signal` are Signals and `r n_watch` are Watches. With this many comparisons, chance alone would produce a few flags (at most about `r round(n_tests * 0.01)` Signals and `r round(n_tests * 0.04)` Watches at these thresholds), so a single flag is a reason to look closer, not proof of a problem.

## Every series, every year

```{ojs}
//| output: false
rows = transpose(sig)
sm = ({
  series: [].concat(smeta.series),
  groups: [].concat(smeta.groups),
  dataTo: [].concat(smeta.dataTo)[0],
  thisYear: [].concat(smeta.thisYear)[0]
})
years = [...new Set(rows.map(d => d.year))].sort((a, b) => a - b)
cellOf = new Map(rows.map(d => [d.name + "|" + d.year, d]))
fmt1 = d3.format(".1f")
```

```{ojs}
html`<p class="dash-note">Each cell is the count of US recall notices that year. <span class="sig-key sig-watch">△ Watch</span> <span class="sig-key sig-signal">▲ Signal</span> Hover for the expected count and limits, and <strong>click a series name</strong> to chart it below.</p>`
```

::: {.column-page}

```{ojs}
{
  const table = html`<table class="sig-table">
    <thead><tr><th></th>${years.map(y => html`<th scope="col">${y === sm.thisYear ? `${String(y).slice(2)}*` : `'${String(y).slice(2)}`}</th>`)}</tr></thead>
    <tbody></tbody>
  </table>`;
  const tbody = table.querySelector("tbody");
  let lastGroup = null;
  sm.series.forEach((name, i) => {
    const group = sm.groups[i];
    if (group !== lastGroup) {
      tbody.append(html`<tr class="sig-group"><th colspan=${years.length + 1}>${group}</th></tr>`);
      lastGroup = group;
    }
    const tr = html`<tr></tr>`;
    const th = html`<th scope="row" tabindex="0" class="sig-name">${name}</th>`;
    const pick = () => { viewof chosen.value = name; viewof chosen.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); };
    th.onclick = pick;
    th.onkeydown = e => { if (e.key === "Enter") pick(); };
    if (name === chosen) th.classList.add("sig-chosen");
    tr.append(th);
    for (const y of years) {
      const d = cellOf.get(name + "|" + y);
      const td = html`<td>${d ? (d.status === "Signal" ? `▲${d.observed}` : d.status === "Watch" ? `△${d.observed}` : d.observed) : ""}</td>`;
      if (d) {
        td.classList.add(d.status === "Signal" ? "sig-signal" : d.status === "Watch" ? "sig-watch" : "sig-none");
        td.title = `${name}, ${d.label}\nObserved: ${d.observed}\nExpected: ${fmt1(d.expected)}\nWatch above ${d.limit95}, Signal above ${d.limit99}\nStatus: ${d.status}`;
      }
      tr.append(td);
    }
    tbody.append(tr);
  });
  const wrap = html`<div class="sig-wrap"></div>`;
  wrap.append(table);
  return wrap;
}
```

:::

```{ojs}
html`<p class="dash-note">* ${sm.thisYear} is year-to-date, to ${sm.dataTo}. Years start in 2005 because each needs five earlier years as its baseline.</p>`
```

## One series over time

```{ojs}
viewof chosen = Inputs.select(sm.series, {label: "Series", value: "All bicycle recalls"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const d = rows.filter(r => r.name === chosen && !r.is_ytd);
  const fig = Plot.plot({
    width,
    height: 320,
    marginLeft: 48,
    x: {label: null, tickFormat: "d"},
    y: {label: "US recall notices per year", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(d, {x: "year", y1: 0, y2: "limit99", fill: "#e8edf1", curve: "step"}),
      Plot.lineY(d, {x: "year", y: "limit95", stroke: "#9aa5ae", strokeDasharray: "4,3", curve: "step"}),
      Plot.lineY(d, {x: "year", y: "expected", stroke: "#5b7083", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      Plot.lineY(d, {x: "year", y: "observed", stroke: "#1f4e79", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.dot(d, {
        x: "year", y: "observed", r: d => d.status === "Expected" ? 3.5 : 6,
        fill: d => d.status === "Signal" ? "#c0392b" : d.status === "Watch" ? "#e3a400" : "#1f4e79",
        stroke: "#ffffff", strokeWidth: 1.5,
        tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.year}: ${d.observed} observed, ${fmt1(d.expected)} expected\nWatch above ${d.limit95}, Signal above ${d.limit99}\n${d.status}`
      }),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  });
  const wrap = html`<div class="dash-chart"></div>`;
  wrap.append(fig);
  return wrap;
}
```

```{ojs}
html`<p class="dash-note">Dark line and dots: observed. Grey line: expected (five-year average). Dashed line: Watch threshold. Shaded area: up to the Signal threshold. Larger amber or red dots are Watches and Signals. The year-to-date figure for ${sm.thisYear} is in the table above, not on this chart, because it covers only part of a year.</p>`
```

::: {.caveat-box}
**What a signal means here.** A signal says a count is unusual for that series, not that products have become less safe. Recalls rise when a regulator focuses on a product type, when a new standard is introduced, or when one large company recalls several models at once. Each signal is a prompt to read the recalls behind it in the [dashboard](dashboard.qmd).
:::
